decision: Recover enough prompt-processing and TTFT performance from the exact PROFILE=fidelity control to pass candidate gates without sacrificing its fidelity, tail, decode, context, or capability envelope.

primary_control.body: all-trellis hydrated K5/K5/K6 MLP with calibrated serialized attention

paired_promotion_gates.fidelity: candidate-blind paired non-inferiority against the exact primary control for mean KLD and frozen tails
paired_promotion_gates.capability: candidate-blind paired non-inferiority against the exact primary control on every retained capability panel
paired_promotion_gates.runtime: same inputs, runtime tree, hardware blocks, warm-up policy, and randomized/interleaved execution
paired_promotion_gates.improvement: material PP/TTFT recovery; absolute PP must still clear 7000 tok/s

secondary_profiles.throughput: performance ceiling and secondary comparator only; never the primary control
secondary_profiles.balanced: secondary comparator only; never the primary control

historical_g0.rule: Historical evidence remains immutable, but this profile cannot substitute for a fresh exact PROFILE=fidelity control in a later campaign.

invariants: The exact PROFILE=fidelity tuple is the primary control even though it fails the absolute 7000 tok/s PP candidate gate.
A baseline reproduction is judged by frozen non-regression tolerances, not by candidate promotion thresholds.
Every embedding, K-map, codebook, topology, runtime flag, kernel route, MTP, KV, graph, or context change is a candidate variable unless it is byte-identical to the frozen control tuple.
No candidate may be promoted from an absolute Gate A pass alone; it must also pass preregistered paired non-inferiority against the exact fidelity control.
The throughput profile cannot replace the fidelity control merely because it already exceeds 7000 tok/s.
Historical receipts are not rewritten to conform to this decision.
